The power method uses exponentiation to normalize inverse-odds into probabilities, ensuring sum-to-one while preserving relative weights. The Shin model introduces an insider-trading parameter z to reflect asymmetric information, mapping odds into risk-neutral probabilities. Buchdahl’s approach adjusts odds directly based on margin, producing fair odds that eliminate overround. Bivariate Poisson provides a stochastic kernel for modeling correlated outcomes in parlays, capturing shared dependencies among events. Each method exhibits different failure modes: power method may suffer from numerical overflow, Shin requires root-finding stability, Buchdahl fails when margin exceeds bounds, and Poisson assumes independence beyond shared components. These primitives collectively enable robust inference in high-dimensional sports markets.
